description: An introduction to statistics covering measures of central tendency (mean, median and mode) for ungrouped and grouped data, including the assumed mean method, modal and median classes, class boundaries and midpoints, and reading the median from a cumulative frequency curve.

mcq.explanation: The sum of the values is 48 and there are 6 values, so the mean is 48/6 = 8. Here 8.5 is the median and 12 is the mode. Exam Tip: the mean is the total divided by how many values there are.
Sorting the values gives 5, 7, 9, 13, 21, and the middle value of these five numbers is 9. Exam Tip: always arrange the data in order before finding the median.
The value 6 appears three times, more often than any other value, so it is the mode. Exam Tip: the mode is the most frequent value, not the average.
With an even number of values, the median is the average of the two middle values, (8 + 10)/2 = 9. Exam Tip: for an even count, average the two central values.

mcq.questionText: A grouped frequency table has classes 0-9, 10-19, 20-29 with frequencies 2, 5, 3 for 10 students. What is the mean score?
mcq.explanation: Using midpoints 4.5, 14.5, 24.5, the sum of fx is 2(4.5) + 5(14.5) + 3(24.5) = 155, so the mean is 155/10 = 15.5. Exam Tip: represent each class by its midpoint before multiplying by the frequency.

mcq.questionText: Using an assumed mean A = 50 for 20 values with a sum of fd equal to 30, find the actual mean.
mcq.explanation: The actual mean is A + (sum of fd)/(sum of f) = 50 + 30/20 = 50 + 1.5 = 51.5. Exam Tip: add the average deviation to the assumed mean.

mcq.questionText: The mean of five numbers is 12. Four of them are 10, 15, 8 and 14. Find the fifth number.
mcq.explanation: The total of the five numbers is 5 x 12 = 60, and the four known values sum to 47, so the fifth is 60 - 47 = 13. Exam Tip: multiply the mean by the count to get the total.

mcq.questionText: A marks table has classes 1-10, 11-20, 21-30, 31-40 with frequencies 3, 7, 6, 4 for 20 students. Which is the median class?
mcq.explanation: Here n/2 = 10, and the cumulative frequencies are 3 then 10, so the 10th value falls in the class 11-20. Exam Tip: the median class is where the cumulative frequency first reaches n/2.

mcq.questionText: The modal class 20-24 has frequency 12, the class before it has frequency 8, the class after it has frequency 6, and the class width is 5. Find the mode.
mcq.explanation: With L = 19.5, d1 = 12 - 8 = 4 and d2 = 12 - 6 = 6, the mode is 19.5 + (4/(4+6)) x 5 = 19.5 + 2 = 21.5. Exam Tip: use the lower boundary of the modal class, not its lower limit.

mcq.questionText: For n = 40, the median class has lower boundary L = 29.5, frequency 10, class width 10 and cumulative frequency before it of 14. Find the median.
mcq.explanation: The median is L + ((n/2 - cf)/f) x c = 29.5 + ((20 - 14)/10) x 10 = 29.5 + 6 = 35.5. Exam Tip: n/2 = 20 here, and cf is the cumulative frequency of the class before the median class.

mcq.questionText: Each of 10 values is increased by 5. What happens to the mean?
mcq.explanation: Adding 5 to every value adds 50 to the total, and 50 divided by 10 values raises the mean by 5. Exam Tip: adding a constant to every value shifts the mean by that same constant.

mcq.questionText: The mean mark of 8 students is 62. What is the total of their marks?
mcq.explanation: The total equals the mean times the number of students, 62 x 8 = 496. Exam Tip: total = mean x number of values.

mcq.questionText: Which measure of central tendency is most affected by an extremely large value?
mcq.explanation: The mean uses every value in its calculation, so a very large outlier pulls it up, while the median and mode are barely affected. Exam Tip: the mean is the least resistant to outliers.

mcq.questionText: In a class, 20 boys have a mean of 60 and 30 girls have a mean of 70. What is the mean for the whole class?
mcq.explanation: The boys total 20 x 60 = 1200 and the girls total 30 x 70 = 2100, so the combined mean is (1200 + 2100)/50 = 3300/50 = 66. Exam Tip: combine totals and counts separately, then divide.

mcq.questionText: On an ogive (cumulative frequency curve) for 40 students, at which cumulative frequency is the median read off?
mcq.explanation: The median on an ogive is read at a cumulative frequency of n/2 = 40/2 = 20. Exam Tip: draw a line across from n/2 on the cumulative frequency axis to find the median.

fib.explanation: The sum is 40 and there are 4 values, so the mean is 40/4 = 10. Exam Tip: divide the total by the number of values.
The value 4 appears three times, more than any other value, so it is the mode. Exam Tip: count how often each value occurs.
Sorted the values are 3, 8, 12, so the middle value is 8. Exam Tip: order the data first, then take the centre value.

fib.questionText: If the mean of 6 numbers is 15, the sum of the numbers is ____.
fib.explanation: The sum equals the mean times the count, 15 x 6 = 90. Exam Tip: sum = mean x number of values.

fib.questionText: The class midpoint of the class 30-39 is ____.
fib.explanation: The midpoint is the average of the class limits, (30 + 39)/2 = 34.5. Exam Tip: add the lower and upper limits and divide by 2.

fib.questionText: In the assumed mean method with A = 50, the deviation d for x = 57 is ____.
fib.explanation: The deviation is d = x - A = 57 - 50 = 7. Exam Tip: subtract the assumed mean from the value.

fib.questionText: For 25 ordered values, the median is the ____th value.
fib.explanation: For an odd count the median position is (n+1)/2 = (25+1)/2 = 13, so it is the 13th value. Exam Tip: use (n+1)/2 to locate the median position.

fib.questionText: If the mean of x, 8 and 12 is 10, then x = ____.
fib.explanation: The total must be 3 x 10 = 30, so x = 30 - 8 - 12 = 10. Exam Tip: multiply the mean by the count, then subtract the known values.

fib.questionText: In a cumulative frequency table, the cumulative frequency of the last class equals the ____.
fib.explanation: Cumulative frequency adds up all frequencies, so by the last class it reaches the total frequency n. Exam Tip: the final cumulative frequency should equal the sum of all frequencies.

fib.questionText: The lower class boundary of the class 40-49 is ____.
fib.explanation: The lower boundary is halfway between 39 and 40, which is 39.5. Exam Tip: subtract 0.5 from the lower limit to get the lower boundary.

tf.questionText: The mode is the value that occurs most frequently in a data set.
tf.explanation: By definition, the mode is the value that appears more often than any other in the data set.

tf.questionText: A data set can have more than one mode.
tf.explanation: If two or more values share the highest frequency, the data set has more than one mode and is called bimodal or multimodal.

tf.questionText: The median of a data set is always one of the values in the data set.
tf.explanation: For an even number of values the median is the average of the two middle values, which may not itself be in the data set.

tf.questionText: The mean of the data 5, 5, 5, 5 is 5.
tf.explanation: The sum is 20 and there are 4 values, so the mean is 20/4 = 5, which matches every value.

tf.questionText: Data must be arranged in order of size before the median can be located.
tf.explanation: The median is the middle value, so the data must first be sorted in order of size to find it.

tf.questionText: When calculating the mean of grouped data, each class is represented by its class midpoint.
tf.explanation: The exact values within a class are unknown, so the midpoint is used to represent the whole class in the calculation.

tf.questionText: The modal class is the class interval with the highest frequency.
tf.explanation: The modal class is defined as the class interval containing the greatest number of values, that is the highest frequency.

tf.questionText: If every value in a data set is increased by 3, the median also increases by 3.
tf.explanation: Adding the same constant to every value shifts the whole ordered data set up by that amount, so the middle value also increases by 3.

tf.questionText: If all data values are whole numbers, the mean must also be a whole number.
tf.explanation: The mean is a total divided by a count, so whole-number data can still give a decimal mean, such as (2 + 3)/2 = 2.5.

tf.questionText: In the assumed mean method, the actual mean is A + (sum of fd divided by sum of f).
tf.explanation: The assumed mean method corrects the guess A by adding the average of the deviations, which is (sum of fd)/(sum of f).

summary.correctAnswer: The sum of all the values divided by the number of values.
summary.explanation: For 2, 4, 6 the sum is 12 and there are 3 values, so the mean is 12/3 = 4. Exam Tip: mean = total divided by count.

summary.correctAnswer: The middle value when the data is arranged in order of size, or the average of the two middle values if there is an even number of them.
summary.explanation: For 3, 8, 9 the median is 8, while for 4, 8, 10, 14 it is (8 + 10)/2 = 9. Exam Tip: always sort the data before locating the middle.

summary.correctAnswer: The value that occurs most frequently in a data set.
summary.explanation: In 6, 6, 6, 7, 9 the value 6 appears most often, so the mode is 6. Exam Tip: the mode is about frequency, not size.

summary.correctAnswer: The sum of frequency times midpoint (sum of fx) divided by the total frequency (sum of f).
summary.explanation: Each class is represented by its midpoint, then mean = (sum of fx)/(sum of f). For midpoints 4.5, 14.5, 24.5 with frequencies 2, 5, 3 the mean is 155/10 = 15.5. Exam Tip: find each midpoint first, then multiply by the frequency.

summary.correctAnswer: A method that finds the mean using mean = A + (sum of fd)/(sum of f), where A is a guessed mean and d = x - A is the deviation.
summary.explanation: With A = 50 and (sum of fd)/(sum of f) = 30/20 = 1.5, the mean is 50 + 1.5 = 51.5. Exam Tip: choose A near the centre to keep the deviations small.

summary.correctAnswer: The class interval that has the highest frequency in a grouped frequency table.
summary.explanation: If the class 20-24 has the greatest frequency of 12, then 20-24 is the modal class. Exam Tip: look for the row with the largest frequency.

summary.correctAnswer: The class interval that contains the (n/2)th value, found using the cumulative frequencies.
summary.explanation: For n = 20, n/2 = 10, and if the cumulative frequencies reach 10 in the class 11-20, that is the median class. Exam Tip: find where the cumulative frequency first reaches n/2.

summary.correctAnswer: The point halfway between the upper limit of one class and the lower limit of the next, removing the gaps between classes.
summary.explanation: For the class 40-49 the lower boundary is 39.5 and the upper boundary is 49.5. Exam Tip: subtract 0.5 from the lower limit and add 0.5 to the upper limit.

summary.correctAnswer: The average of the lower and upper class limits, used to represent the class.
summary.explanation: For the class 30-39 the midpoint is (30 + 39)/2 = 34.5. Exam Tip: add the two limits and divide by 2.

summary.correctAnswer: A running total of frequencies up to the upper boundary of each class, which is plotted to draw an ogive curve.
summary.explanation: The last cumulative frequency equals the total frequency n, and the median is read from the ogive at n/2. Exam Tip: plot cumulative frequency against the upper class boundaries.

hoq.questionText: A grouped table has marks 10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49 with frequencies 4, 6, 10, 5 for 25 students. What is the mean mark?
hoq.explanation: The midpoints are 14.5, 24.5, 34.5, 44.5. Multiplying by the frequencies gives 4(14.5) + 6(24.5) + 10(34.5) + 5(44.5) = 58 + 147 + 345 + 222.5 = 772.5. Dividing by 25 gives a mean of 772.5/25 = 30.9. Option A wrongly uses the lower class limits instead of the midpoints. Exam Tip: use the class midpoints, not the lower limits.

hoq.questionText: Using the same table (marks 10-19, 20-29, 30-39, 40-49 with frequencies 4, 6, 10, 5 for 25 students), what is the median mark?
hoq.explanation: Here n/2 = 12.5, and the cumulative frequencies are 4, 10, 20, so the median falls in the class 30-39. With L = 29.5, cf before = 10, f = 10 and c = 10, the median is 29.5 + ((12.5 - 10)/10) x 10 = 29.5 + 2.5 = 32. Exam Tip: use the lower boundary 29.5, not the limit 30.

hoq.questionText: Fatuma records her six daily sales in thousand Tsh as 40, 55, 45, 40, 60, 48. What are the mean, median and mode?
hoq.explanation: The mean is 288/6 = 48. Sorting gives 40, 40, 45, 48, 55, 60, so the median is (45 + 48)/2 = 46.5. The value 40 occurs twice, so the mode is 40. Exam Tip: the mode is the most frequent value, not the largest.
